clue.text: Make merry, take in a show

indicators.note: to take in is to swallow or enclose, so the merrymaking word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: to make merry is to revel

explanation.surface: A night out: celebrating and catching a show along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to disclose it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: We must top and tail these earthbound creatures

indicators.note: topping and tailing removes the first and last letters of the words We must, leaving the inner run

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim these flightless birds, as if preparing vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a command to the birds; it is an instruction to drop W and T from WEMUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless birds, so they are tied to the ground.

clue.text: Return to the country, the scene of the crime

definitions.text: Return to the country, the scene of the crime

parts.words: Return to the country, the scene of the crime
parts.note: describes the legal process of sending an accused person back to the state where the offence took place

explanation.surface: Sounds like a criminal revisiting the scene, or a holiday back home.
explanation.definitionFit: Extradition is the formal handing over of a suspect to the jurisdiction where the crime was committed.

clue.text: A poet not out after a spree

indicators.note: after places the not-out piece behind the spree piece

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun, a spree
a batsman who is not out in cricket is still in

explanation.surface: A poet still standing after a night on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: Philip LARKIN was an English poet. In cricket a batsman who is 'not out' is still IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was a celebrated twentieth-century English poet, so the answer is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Plump for pudding

definitions.meaning: a British steamed or baked suet pudding with jam rolled up in it

explanation.surface: Choosing dessert, or describing someone who ate it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump for' looks like a phrase meaning 'choose'; here 'for' is a link between the two definitions. The pudding is a jam-filled suet roll, a British school-dinner classic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a chubby person and a rolled jam suet pudding.

clue.text: Make love?

parts.note: love read as a score of zero, so making something love means bringing it to zero

explanation.surface: A romantic suggestion, or a coy question.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis 'love' is a score of nil, so to make something love is to bring it down to zero.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something down to nil is to make it into a score of love, the tennis zero.

clue.text: Makes fun of politician seen in saloon, drunk

indicators.note: a thing seen in another is placed within it
drunk suggests the letters reeling about into a new order

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Satirists mock an MP spotted intoxicated in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' signals the anagram of the bar word, and 'seen in' places the politician inside; the bar word itself is not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon is to ridicule or satirise, so lampoons means makes fun of.

clue.text: Policeman held up in a state of terror

indicators.note: something held is gripped within the other piece

parts.note: PC, police constable

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words in a are read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A constable taken hostage in a state of fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the clue's own words 'in a' (a down-clue convention), and 'held' places them inside the constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, a state of terror.

clue.text: Canal employee identified by hair and ring

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair
a keeper is a ring worn to hold another ring in place

explanation.surface: A canal worker recognised by hairstyle and a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: A keeper is a guard ring worn to stop a wedding ring slipping off.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock-keeper is employed to operate the gates of a canal lock.

clue.text: How to serve toast, say, when retired?

definitions.text: How to serve toast, say, when retired?

parts.words: How to serve toast, say, when retired?
parts.note: toast is typically served spread with a dairy fat; when retired suggests breakfast taken in bed

explanation.surface: A question about breakfast in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast is commonly served with butter spread on it, so it comes buttered.

clue.text: I eat out in foreign capital

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the eating word goes round the letter

parts.note: to munch is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone dining out in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eat out' looks like dining at a restaurant, but 'out' tells you MUNCH goes outside I. Munich is the capital of Bavaria.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich is the capital of the German state of Bavaria, a capital city abroad.

clue.text: Simple part of the pastry cook's work

definitions.text: part of the pastry cook's work
definitions.meaning: literally a portion of something baked

explanation.surface: A baker's job described as easy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means something very easy, and literally a portion of a baked item.

clue.text: He's on the way to work

definitions.text: He's on the way to work

parts.words: He's on the way to work
parts.note: read as a commuter, but means a man whose work is done on the road surface itself

explanation.surface: A commuter heading to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A road-mender repairs road surfaces, so his work is literally on the way.

clue.text: Withdrawal of 101 meeting points

indicators.note: a withdrawal draws back, so the word of is read backwards

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A course code, perhaps, retreating to its meeting places.
explanation.definitionFit: Foci are points where lines or rays converge, so they are meeting points.

clue.text: Drastic cuts in the monastic establishment

definitions.text: Drastic cuts in the monastic establishment

parts.words: Drastic cuts in the monastic establishment
parts.note: reads as budget cuts at a monastery, but means the shaving of monks' heads

explanation.surface: Austerity cuts imposed on a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsures are the shaved crowns of monks' heads, quite literally severe haircuts in a religious house.

clue.text: Continued, oddly enough, to be missed

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters arranged in a strange new way

explanation.surface: Something that kept going yet strangely went unseen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnoticed was not observed, so it was missed.

clue.text: Dreaming about being in easy reach of a gun

definitions.text: in easy reach of a gun

indicators.note: about here means scattered around, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daydreamer drifting into a gunman's sights.
explanation.definitionFit: A target at mid-range is neither far nor close, within comfortable shooting distance.

clue.text: So he and I form a strong attachment

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people who bond closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is part of the fodder here: SOHEANDI rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is the act of sticking firmly together, a strong attachment.

clue.text: Trotsky came back for the festival

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Leon Trotsky, the Russian revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary returns for the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another word for Christmas, the festive season.

clue.text: One who cares to make an offer

definitions.meaning: someone who looks after something, as in a bartender
to propose a bid or payment

explanation.surface: A carer offering help.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is one who looks after, and to tender is to offer formally.

clue.text: Retire from one's position in hostility

definitions.text: Retire from one's position in hostility

parts.words: Retire from one's position in hostility
parts.note: describes an army withdrawing from its ground during fighting

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a job amid a hostile atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat a retreat is to withdraw hastily, especially from battle.

clue.text: Discrimination makes sense

definitions.meaning: refined judgement in matters of style
one of the five senses, perceiving flavour

explanation.surface: A remark that being discerning is sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste means both discerning judgement and the sense of flavour.

clue.text: Damage one's shed, sadly

definitions.meaning: a drop from the eye shed in sorrow

explanation.surface: A garden shed ruined, to someone's dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut; it is the verb, as in shedding a drop from the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rip and a drop wept in sorrow, pronounced differently.

clue.text: The single boy in a family is very much a favourite

parts.note: odd as in single, unpaired, like an odd sock
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: An only child being the family favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The', 'in a family is' are padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on describes a betting favourite whose chance is better than even.

clue.text: Shown to have a deficit and charged

indicators.note: a deficit is a shortfall, so the word is short of the named letter

parts.note: indicated means shown

explanation.surface: Someone found to be in debt and then formally accused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deficit' looks financial but tells you INDICATED lacks the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Indicted means formally charged with a serious crime.

clue.text: Breakfast ingredient fresh from the fridge, for example

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: e.g., exempli gratia

explanation.surface: Something just taken out of the fridge to cook for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh from' looks like a description of chilled food; 'fresh' rearranges FRIDGE plus EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried egg is a staple item of a cooked breakfast.

clue.text: They sit for qualifications

definitions.meaning: people sitting astride horses or bikes
clauses added to a document that modify it

explanation.surface: Students sitting exams for their qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sit for qualifications' looks like taking exams. A rider is an added clause qualifying a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders sit on horses, and riders are added conditions that qualify an agreement.
